# OCR benchmark

Character error rate (CER) per OCR engine per exhibit type.

```
make ocr-bench                                   # all configured engines, synthetic manifest
python eval/ocr_bench/bench.py --engines tesseract,azure_di --save-db
```

Output: `var/out/ocr_bench/report.md` (table) and `results.json` (per page); `--save-db` also writes
`eval_runs` + `ocr_benchmark_results`.

## Page sets

* `manifest.json` — generated by `eval/samples/generate_samples.py` (36 synthetic pages, exact ground truth).
  `text_layer` scores ~0 here by construction; use it only to sanity-check the harness.
* `real/manifest.json` — **hand-transcribed real pages (not yet created)**. Put scans in `real/pages/`
  and transcriptions in `real/transcriptions/<id>.txt`, one entry per page:

```json
{"pages": [{"id": "PILOT-0001-p03", "pdf": "ocr_bench/real/pages/0001.pdf", "page_index": 2,
            "exhibit_type": "PROPERTY_CARD", "transcription_file": "transcriptions/PILOT-0001-p03.txt",
            "data_class": "real"}]}
```

Real pages carry `data_class: real`, so they are only ever sent to engines approved for real data
(Azure Document Intelligence / Azure OpenAI Regional in Central India, or local Tesseract).
Do not commit real pages to git (`eval/ocr_bench/real/` is git-ignored).

Transcription rules: transcribe exactly what is printed, line by line, in Unicode Devanagari; keep
Devanagari vs ASCII digits as printed; skip stamps/handwriting you cannot read and mark with `�`.
